input.quote: 28.1 This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles.
input.rationale: Section 28.1 selects New York law (with CISG excluded), and Section 28.2 gives the state and federal courts in New York County exclusive jurisdiction, with each Party submitting to personal jurisdiction and waiving venue/forum objections. The only carve-out is the customary right to seek temporary injunctive relief elsewhere to protect confidential information or IP, which does not defeat the exclusive merits forum. A document-wide search found no arbitration provision, no foreign seat, and no competing governing-law or venue clause; Section 28.3's executive-escalation step is a pre-filing meet-and-confer that expressly does not delay urgent relief or limitations-period filings. This sits at the preferred position (New York law, New York County courts), so no redline is proposed.

mappings.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
mappings.quote: This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York

mappings.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
mappings.quote: The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction, and each Party irrevocably submits to personal jurisdiction and waives any objection based on venue or inconvenient forum. Nothing prevents a Party from seeking temporary injunctive relief in another court with jurisdiction to protect confidential information or intellectual property.
